source.note: 英文逐字稿取自 YouTube 字幕；中文為學習用翻譯。版權屬原作者，僅供個人學習。

lines.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.
lines.zh: 哈囉，這裡是 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》。我是 Neil。

lines.en: And I'm Pippa.
lines.zh: 我是 Pippa。

lines.en: Are you good at saving money, Neil?
lines.zh: Neil，你很會存錢嗎？

lines.en: Or do you like to spend it?
lines.zh: 還是你比較喜歡花錢？

lines.en: Well, actually, a bit of both.
lines.zh: 嗯，其實兩者都有一點。

lines.en: I like to spend money on nice things, but I also try to save, mainly because I've got children.
lines.zh: 我喜歡花錢買好東西，但我也會試著存錢，主要是因為我有小孩。

lines.en: How about you?
lines.zh: 你呢？

lines.en: Yeah, I'm the same.
lines.zh: 對，我也一樣。

lines.en: I like to save money, or I try to, for the future.
lines.zh: 我喜歡存錢，或者說我會試著存錢，為了將來。

lines.en: But I also do spend it.
lines.zh: 但我也確實會花錢。

lines.en: I don't count every penny that I spend and save every single penny that I earn.
lines.zh: 我不會精打細算每一分花掉的錢，也不會把賺到的每一分錢都存起來。

lines.en: Mmm. Well, whether you're a saver or a spender, being in debt is common in the UK.
lines.zh: 嗯。不管你是愛存錢還是愛花錢，負債在英國都很常見。

lines.en: Debt refers to money a person has borrowed to buy something and which they have to pay back, usually to a bank, a credit card company, or another person.
lines.zh: Debt（債務）是指一個人為了買東西而借的錢，之後必須還，通常是還給銀行、信用卡公司或其他人。

lines.en: Many people avoid talking about debt, but it affects us all.
lines.zh: 很多人避免談論債務，但它影響我們所有人。

lines.en: In 2025, over 1,000 people contacted the UK Citizens Advice Bureau every single day of the year for help with their debt.
lines.zh: 2025 年，一整年每一天都有超過 1,000 人聯絡英國公民諮詢局，尋求債務方面的協助。

lines.en: And when debt gets out of control, it causes stress and worry.
lines.zh: 當債務失控時，就會造成壓力和擔憂。

lines.en: BBC Radio 4 programme Thinking Allowed interviewed one young man, Jason, about his debt.
lines.zh: BBC 第四電台節目《Thinking Allowed》訪問了一位年輕人 Jason，談他的債務。

lines.en: Whatever jobs there are aren't enough to provide for a family.
lines.zh: 現有的工作都不足以養家。

lines.en: Sometimes you need to take out loans.
lines.zh: 有時候就得去借貸。

lines.en: I've done it a few times, but you can't ever pay it back.
lines.zh: 我借過好幾次，但怎麼樣都還不完。

lines.en: You can't see a way out, other than winning the lottery or something.
lines.zh: 你看不到出路，除非中樂透之類的。

lines.en: I'd like to think I could clear them all one day, even if it means, like, five years paying them off.
lines.zh: 我希望有一天能把它們全部還清，就算要花五年慢慢還也好。

lines.en: Jason uses three phrases, pay back, pay off, and clear debt, all of which mean the same thing – to give back the money you've borrowed.
lines.zh: Jason 用了三個片語：pay back、pay off 和 clear debt，意思都一樣——把借來的錢還回去。

lines.en: In this episode, we'll hear more about living with debt by learning some useful new words and phrases.
lines.zh: 在這一集，我們會透過學習一些實用的新單字和片語，聽到更多關於與債務共處的內容。

lines.en: And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary used, plus a quiz and worksheet, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 別忘了，所有用到的詞彙以及測驗和學習單，都在我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com。

lines.en: But first, I have a question for you, Pippa.
lines.zh: 不過首先，Pippa，我有個問題要問你。

lines.en: According to debt support group The Money Charity, roughly how much is the average British adult in debt through credit cards, overdrafts and personal loans?
lines.zh: 根據債務支援團體 The Money Charity 的資料，英國成年人平均透過信用卡、透支和個人貸款，大約負債多少？

lines.en: Hmm. I'm not sure.
lines.zh: 嗯。我不確定。

lines.en: I'll say £2,200.
lines.zh: 我選 2,200 英鎊。

lines.en: OK.
lines.zh: 好。

lines.en: Well, we will find out the answer later in the programme.
lines.zh: 我們會在節目稍後揭曉答案。

lines.en: Jason's story features in a new book by sociologist Ryan Davey.
lines.zh: Jason 的故事出現在社會學家 Ryan Davey 的新書裡。

lines.en: Ryan spent months living in a low-income housing estate, which he gave the fictional name Woldham.
lines.zh: Ryan 花了好幾個月住在一個低收入住宅社區，他給這個地方取了一個虛構的名字：Woldham。

lines.en: He talked with residents and listened to their money worries.
lines.zh: 他和居民聊天，聽他們對錢的煩惱。

lines.en: Here, Ryan explains more to BBC Radio 4's Thinking Allowed: My approach was to let people know that I was interested in learning about their lives and how they were making ends meet, so I did some interviews with residents, and I paid attention to where debt came up in everyday conversations.
lines.zh: 這是 Ryan 對 BBC 第四電台《Thinking Allowed》的進一步說明：我的做法是讓大家知道我有興趣了解他們的生活，以及他們如何勉強維持收支，所以我訪問了一些居民，並留意債務在日常對話中出現的地方。

lines.en: For many people in Woldham, Jason included, debt was an ordinary feature of daily life.
lines.zh: 對 Woldham 的很多人來說，包括 Jason，債務是日常生活中很普通的一部分。

lines.en: And beyond that, being in arrears – so, being behind with one or more monthly payment commitments – was part of daily life.
lines.zh: 不只如此，拖欠款項——也就是一項或多項每月該付的款項沒有按時繳——也是日常生活的一部分。

lines.en: The people of Woldham were making ends meet.
lines.zh: Woldham 的居民都在 making ends meet。

lines.en: To make ends meet means having just enough money to pay for basic living expenses like food, bills and rent.
lines.zh: To make ends meet 的意思是錢剛好夠支付食物、帳單、房租等基本生活開銷。

lines.en: Ryan found that many residents were in arrears, a phrase meaning to still owe money that should have already been repaid.
lines.zh: Ryan 發現很多居民都 in arrears，這個說法的意思是仍欠著早就該還的錢。

lines.en: For most residents, debt was a normal part of daily life.
lines.zh: 對大多數居民來說，債務是日常生活很正常的一部分。

lines.en: With a regular income, debt can be managed, but for those who are unemployed or on low incomes, it can cause serious distress.
lines.zh: 有固定收入的話，債務還能管理，但對失業或低收入的人來說，它可能造成嚴重的困擾。

lines.en: Here, Ryan discusses how the residents he met felt about their debt with BBC Radio 4's Thinking Allowed: Jason actually fluctuated between wanting to clear all of his debts on the one hand, and on the other what he described as living on the never-never,
lines.zh: 在這裡，Ryan 在 BBC 第四電台《Thinking Allowed》中談到他遇到的居民對債務的感受：Jason 其實在兩種想法之間搖擺，一方面想把所有債務還清，另一方面則是他所說的「living on the never-never」（靠分期過日子），

lines.en: and actually questioning the supposed moral obligation to pay his debts.
lines.zh: 甚至開始質疑所謂償還債務的道德義務。

lines.en: Over the months that I knew him, the financial strain on him and his partner increased.
lines.zh: 在我認識他的那幾個月裡，他和伴侶的經濟壓力越來越大。

lines.en: They missed some of their bills.
lines.zh: 他們漏繳了一些帳單。

lines.en: Their internet was disconnected.
lines.zh: 他們的網路被斷線了。

lines.en: Jason was living on the never-never, an informal phrase for buying the things you need by making regular small payments over a long time.
lines.zh: Jason 過著 living on the never-never 的生活，這是一個非正式的說法，指靠長期定期小額付款來買需要的東西。

lines.en: It's called the never-never because it seems the debt will never be repaid.
lines.zh: 之所以叫 never-never，是因為這筆債好像永遠還不完。

lines.en: Jason experienced financial strain – emotional stress caused by a lack of money to meet his basic needs or to repay his debt.
lines.zh: Jason 承受著 financial strain——因為沒錢滿足基本需求或還債而產生的情緒壓力。

lines.en: Debt is a serious issue.
lines.zh: 債務是一個嚴重的問題。

lines.en: It affects many people and there are support groups who can help if you need it.
lines.zh: 它影響很多人，如果你需要，也有支援團體可以幫忙。

lines.en: OK. Neil, what was the answer to your question?
lines.zh: 好。Neil，你的問題答案是什麼？

lines.en: I asked what the average amount of debt a British adult has through credit cards, overdrafts and personal loans.
lines.zh: 我問的是英國成年人透過信用卡、透支和個人貸款的平均負債金額。

lines.en: I said it was around £2,200.
lines.zh: 我說大約 2,200 英鎊。

lines.en: I'm afraid that's not the right answer.
lines.zh: 很遺憾，這不是正確答案。

lines.en: In fact, it's £4,232. OK.
lines.zh: 事實上是 4,232 英鎊。好。

lines.en: Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with debt – money a person has borrowed and needs to give back.
lines.zh: 我們來複習學到的詞彙，首先是 debt——一個人借來、需要還的錢。

lines.en: The phrases to pay back, to pay off, and to clear a debt all mean to give back money you have borrowed.
lines.zh: to pay back、to pay off 和 to clear a debt 這幾個片語，意思都是把借來的錢還回去。

lines.en: If someone is making ends meet, they have just enough money to pay for basic living expenses.
lines.zh: 如果某人 making ends meet，就是他們的錢剛好夠支付基本生活開銷。

lines.en: And if they are in arrears, they still owe money that should have been repaid already.
lines.zh: 如果他們 in arrears，就是他們仍欠著早就該還的錢。

lines.en: If you buy something on the never-never, you buy it by making small regular payments over a long period.
lines.zh: 如果你 on the never-never 買東西，就是用長期定期小額付款的方式購買。

lines.en: And finally, financial strain is emotional stress caused by a lack of money to meet your basic needs.
lines.zh: 最後，financial strain 是因為沒錢滿足基本需求而產生的情緒壓力。

lines.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you'd like to know how debt is spelled and all the other words from this episode, visit our website, bbclearningenglish.com, to find a full vocabulary list.
lines.zh: 我們的六分鐘又到了，但如果你想知道 debt 怎麼拼，以及這一集的其他單字，可以到我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com 查看完整單字表。

lines.en: See you again soon.
lines.zh: 很快再見。

lines.en: But for now, it's goodbye.
lines.zh: 但現在要說再見了。

lines.en: Bye!
lines.zh: 拜拜！
